title: Janapada of Surasena
capsule: Surasena was one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas of Iron Age northern India, centred on the sacred city of Mathura on the Yamuna River and ruled by the Yadava clans, the Vrishnis and Andhakas. The Anguttara Nikaya, the Ramayana, and the Mahabharata all attest to its prominence, and its association with the Krishna-Vasudeva cult was later noted by Greek writers, who rendered its people as Sourasenoi and Mathura as Methora. In Buddhist tradition King Avantiputta of Surasena appears as a patron of the elder Maha Kaccana during the Buddha's lifetime, marking the kingdom as an important node in the early spread of the new teaching. Through the fifth century BCE it remained a self-standing janapada, before being drawn into the orbit of the expanding Magadhan power to its east in the following century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries are derived solely from textual sources; no archaeological survey has delimited the janapada's extent, and estimates range across the broader Braj region.
